Everyone in China says ‘ecosystem, ecosystem, ecosystem.’ Foundery is a small attempt at trying to build that for consumer brands in India. Korea exported culture. Then the world bought Korean… India has Bollywood, music, food, fashion, yoga and Ayurveda, a cultural moat very few countries can replicate.. Maybe we need to stop thinking only about exporting products and start deliberately exporting India. Consumer brands could follow.

The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function.” — F. Scott Fitzgerald The internet increasingly rewards the angrier, louder side, the more certain-sounding side, often the stupider side. Maybe intelligence is being able to understand why the other side believes what it believes. Introducing WTF: Discourse. Two opposing ideas. Two people who actually believe them. No winner. Just the strongest version of both arguments. You decide what you believe.

Same family? Nope. Same childhood? Absolutely not. Parents show up differently for each child depending on the season of their life, their relationship, and even their financial situation. It’s not about who is loved more. It’s about how that love is expressed — and how each child experiences it. If you’ve ever wondered why you and your siblings remember childhood so differently — this is why. This clip is

He is fascinated by the people and organizations that make the greatest, lasting impact on the world. He h

Founder @ The Curve (Sep 2021 - Present 5 years 2 months) — We imagine a world in which all people feel justice is administered with dignity, equity and fairness. The Curve is a 501(c)3 organization dedicated to making this vision a reality. Please visit thecurve.org to learn more.

Host, A Bit of Optimism podcast @ Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company (2020 - Present 6 years) — During these times, we are all having to find new ways to connect. Join me every week as I talk with people that inspire me about love, life, leadership, and silver linings. The hope is that we all leave with something I think we need these days... A Bit of Optimism.Listen online at https://simonsinek.com/podcast/ or wherever you get your podcasts.

Founder and Visionary @ Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company (2007 - Present 19 years) — We imagine a world where the vast majority of people wake up every day feeling inspired, feel safe at work, and fulfilled at the end of the day. My team and I believe in this bright future and our ability to build it together.Get tools and resources to inspire at simonsinek.com.

As an unshakeable optimist, he believes in our ability to build this world together.A trained ethnographer, Simon is fascinated by the people and organizations that make the greatest and longest-lasting impact. li.name: Arianna Huffington
li.headline: Founder and CEO at Thrive Global | Passionate about Health and AI
li.about: I’m the founder and CEO of Thrive Global, a behavior change technology company with the mission of improving health and helping us move from merely surviving to thriving. I also founded The Huffington Post and have written 15 books, including Thrive and The Sleep Revolution.I’m originally from Greece (and still have the accent to prove it!). When I was 17, I moved to England and studied economics at Cambridge University, where I frankly spent most of my time debating at the Cambridge Union.I live in New York but also spend time in Los Angeles, and love being a Yiayia (Greek for grandmother) to my almost three-year-old grandson Alexander and his newborn sister Annabel.My journey to focusing on health began with a fall. In April 2007, I collapsed from exhaustion and burnout and hit my head on my desk on the way down, breaking my cheekbone. In the wake of my fall, I found myself going from doctor to doctor to find out what was wrong. Doctors’ waiting rooms were good places for me to ask myself a lot of questions about the kind of life I was living.After all the tests, it turned out nothing was wrong. Except for the fact that everything was wrong. I was suffering from an acute case of burnout. I had bought into the myth that burnout was the price I had to pay for success. I became more and more passionate about the five daily habits that drive so much of our health: nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and connection. That led me to write Thrive and The Sleep Revolution. The books struck a chord, but I wanted to go beyond speaking and writing to helping people move from awareness to action. So in 2016 I founded Thrive Global, which helps people transform their health by combining Microsteps — small, science-backed daily steps — with technology, storytelling and community. And last year, with the OpenAI Startup Fund, we launched Thrive AI Health to build an AI health coach to democratize access to health coaching.

caption: The problem with loyalty to a company is that it often doesn't go both ways. So, be sure you're not working yourself to death. Don't let work cause you to miss dinners, skip workouts, not see your family, or miss out on that vacation. None of that stuff proves you're “committed to the mission." li.name: Justin Welsh
li.headline: Writer & Entrepreneur. I write The Saturday Essay for 200,000+ ambitious people living and working on their own terms.
li.about: For more than a decade, I lived the kind of life ambitious people are told to want. I helped build two companies past $1B in valuation and raised more than $300M in venture capital. By 33, I was Chief Revenue Officer at a venture-backed company, making more money than I’d ever imagined. And quietly falling apart.I was burned out, anxious, drinking too much, and increasingly convinced that if I kept going, I might not see fifty.Then one afternoon, in our house in Los Angeles, I had a panic attack so severe I ended up on the kitchen floor. My wife, Jennifer, called 911. The paramedics came. And by the time they were standing in our home, it was impossible to keep pretending this was just stress.When it passed, I knew that the life I was building wasn’t the one I wanted to live.So Jennifer and I quit our high-paying jobs with almost no plan. We bought a house in the mountains of Upstate New York, drove across the country, and started our lives over.In the years since, I’ve built a $15M one-person business with no employees and no investors, and an audience of 1.5M+ people has followed along. But that’s not the real story.The real story is that I got my life back, slowly, unglamorously, one difficult choice at a time.Today, I spend that life writing.Every Saturday, I publish one essay about the choices that made it possible: leaving the obvious path, redefining ambition, using money for freedom instead of performance, and building something of your own without letting it consume you.These are the choices that can look wrong from the outside and still be right for the life you actually want.If that’s the kind of conversation you’ve been wanting to have with yourself, I’d love to have you with us.

li.about: Gary Vaynerchuk is a serial entrepreneur and serves as the Chairman of VaynerX, the CEO of VaynerMedia, and Creator and CEO of VeeFriends, and 6x New York Times Best Selling Author. Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet. Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber. Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has ofﬁces in Amsterdam, Bangkok, Chicago, Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, New York, Tokyo, Toronto, Singapore, and Sydney. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX modern-day parent company, which also includes Eva Nosidam Productions, Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, VaynerSpeakers, VaynerCommerce, Tamara Group, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League. Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 50 million followers and garner more than 2+ billion impressions per year across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally. Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, The Paley Center, and Pencils of Promise. He is also an advisor for District and a longtime Well Member of charity: water. Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets.

li.headline: Founder and Chairwoman of Acquisition.com
li.about:
Leila Hormozi is an entrepreneur, investor, and Chairwoman of Acquisition.com, a $200M+ portfolio of companies she co-founded with her husband. She also serves as a managing partner across multiple ventures, spanning advisory services, media, and technology.

Leila is considered one of the leading voices on scaling organizations, leadership, and building enduring companies. She is recognized for her ability to distill complex systems into practical frameworks leaders can use to build teams, drive growth, and create sustainable competitive advantage. Her approach sits at the intersection of business strategy, psychology, and operational excellence.

Known for her candid and direct style, she has become a trusted voice to entrepreneurs, CEOs, and operators worldwide. She brings brand relevance and competitive greatness to the forefront by combining deep operational expertise with forward-thinking cultural insights.

Leila is also an active investor and advisor, with stakes in a diverse set of businesses across software, consumer, and services. Through Acquisition.com, she and her team help founders grow from $3M to $30M and beyond, equipping them with the infrastructure, playbooks, and leadership capacity to scale.

In addition to running multiple companies, Leila shares her experiences and lessons openly through her podcast, videos, and writing, reaching millions of founders and operators globally each month. Her work has positioned her as a modern architect of business education - part operator, part strategist, part coach.

Leila’s mission is to build Acquisition.com into the “Disney of Business” a brand ecosystem that helps entrepreneurs at every stage unlock their potential, while setting the highest standard for what it means to build enduring, principled companies.

caption: ✨🦄 NEW PR AT THE BOSTON MARATHON!!! 🦄✨ 3:27:37 7:55/mile pace Four minute PR from my best previous time at Berlin 2024 Honestly, still speechless over this. I cannot believe that at age 44, one week after a 100k race, five months post-injury…that this happened. An entire marathon at a mile pace that starts with a 7! A Boston Qualifying time AT BOSTON! And to do this with my son here with me! OMFG!!! Have been working so so hard, and it doesn’t always come together on race day. But when it does…there’s no feeling quite like it. Time to go eat all the food and cry so many happy tears. | date: 2026-04-20

caption: Fastest Known Time on the Baja Sur 135km Trail! On March 6, I attempted the Fastest Known Time (FKT) for Mexico’s 135km Baja Sur Trail across the entire Baja Sur Peninsula. 82 miles from the Pacific Ocean → Sea of Cortez. 13,000 feet of elevation. One absolutely savage mountain section from miles 17–34 that climbed 6,000 feet in just 6 miles — including three straight miles at 30% grade in peak heat. 40 miles through night under the moon and stars. One 5-minute dirt nap after mile 60. And a sunrise at mile 70 that made the entire effort feel almost spiritual. My first “comeback” ultra distance | date: 2026-03-07

caption: Officially a @cocodona250 finisher. Still processing the experience and will have a more in depth post soon, but for now: 257 miles across Arizona 36,000+ feet of elevation 6 total hours of sleep across 5 days Torrential rain, insane heat, snow, lightning & hail Insane amounts of Coca Cola & cookies consumed 65 miles done on a busted shin/ankle Hysterical laugher and full body crying Met my own soul (several times) Literally the greatest friends on the planet An accomplishment nobody can ever take from me 📷: @howiesternphoto @ekzooks | date: 2025-05-10

caption: My ginormous baby is TWELVE today!!! 🥹🎂❤️ We are celebrating with a mother-son adventure in Chicago! A weekend of running, matching outfits, deep dish pizza, friends and birthday surprises. Happy birthday, Simi! I love watching you grow up, even if I wish you’d slow down just a tiny bit. (Vertically and literally) | date: 2026-10-10

PRs. Podiums. Long runs. Matching outfits. Donuts. I fear I have created exactly | date: 2026-10-04

caption: Miami 100 mile ultra. First place female and second fastest female time ever! Miami, you were beautiful, painful, chaotic, insane and amazing in all the best ways. The race was an adventure-style checkpoint race, where you didn’t learn the course until you were in it, and you got the directions for each checkpoint in real time. I ran over bridges, around islands, through neighborhoods, and navigated crowded touristy areas. All in hot and crazy humid Florida weather. When @joecorcione said he thought I was capable of running a ~20 hour 100 miler time (roughly a 12 minute mile, including stops)  | date: 2026-09-27

caption: The past few days have seen some fun milestones!! 🍊 My 1,000th OrangeTheory class! I walked into OTF almost four years ago with no clue how that gym would change my life. Countless 6am classes, some of my closest friendships, big goals dreamt & done, and a whole lot of life lived under those orange lights. Naturally, we celebrated the only reasonable way: a 6am toga party. 🔥 My son’s new 5k PR! I got to run side by side in matching outfits with my son Simi, as he dug so deep and set a new PR on the exact same course where he last set a PR at this distance, two years ago. Super proud mom. Eve | date: 2026-09-24

caption: Apparently tapering for a race doesn’t HAVE to be a disaster. (Who knew?) This week included: 70 miles, an actual full rest day (!!) and a truly unreasonable amount of fun: 👫 Doubles HYROX with my husband — we crushed our goals and had an absolute blast. Thank goodness for his ability to pull a sled and let me passenger princess that one… 🏃‍♀️ A long run to visit a friend, because apparently I now make house calls by foot 🏃‍♂️ Intervals with rock star friend + pacer Ben, who for some reason, continues to voluntarily participate in my nonsense 😂 An “apology tour” park loop — because deep co | date: 2026-09-13

caption: 93 miles this week in the most unhinged, fun, “Randi” way ever 🏃‍♀️ Monday: A new 50K PR in a time trial with @dr.joelipsky biking alongside me for all 31.1 miles 🌙 Thursday (Weds night?): An all-out 1-mile race through Times Square at 1AM with my son @orchardstreetrunners absolutely epic OSR1 🎥: Also Thursday: Live taping of a Peloton tread class with @mattwilpers 💪 Friday: A solo HYROX with @sydneysmith812 — and my husband cheering. And then getting to cheer for him! 🏅 Sunday: Carderock Trail Half Marathon in 1:45:43 — 4th place woman, 1st in my age group! Thanks @bishopseventsllc for t | date: 2026-09-06

caption: Normal mother-son activities: dinner, movies, a board game Us: racing one mile at 1am through Times Square 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️ Do I have a mini me or what?! 😂 Some families make memories during normal waking hours. We are not those families. Thanks @orchardstreetrunners for the awesome vibes and great memories. Side note: Both Asher and I got PRs in the mile! Asher ran a 5:05 and I ran a 6:24! | date: 2026-09-03

caption: I’ve been thinking a LOT about pressure lately. The pressure to perform. To lead. To win. To keep going when things get hard. And, as someone who thinks running 100 miles is a reasonable recreational activity 😂, I’m endlessly fascinated by the question: What makes some people extraordinarily good under pressure? I’m SO excited to share that after twelve years of my business talk radio show on SiriusXM, our show is back better than ever for our thirteenth year with a whole new relaunch: 🎙️ UNDER PRESSURE with Randi Zuckerberg I’ll be sitting down with some of the mentally toughest people I kn | date: 2026-09-02

caption: I found a new puzzle and I’m having so much fun being a beginner at it! Rather than get increasingly good at surviving ridiculously long distances, @dr.joelipsky and I schemed that maybe this should be the summer of seeing how fast I could learn to run the 50k distance. It’s a deceiving distance - on the surface, it’s “only five miles longer than the marathon” - but in reality, those five extra miles feel like a whole entire marathon in themselves. Earlier in the summer, I ran a time trial 50k on a bike path, with Joe supporting me on the bike, and finished in 4:44 (a 9:07/mile pace). I loved  | date: 2026-09-01

Whether embarking on spontaneous backpack trips around the world, training martial arts, or coding late in the lab, he values humility, deep conversations, quiet hikes, and sharing memorable street-food dates.

Driven by a desire to explore the mysteries of the universe, engineering, and human nature, he balances deep philosophical intellectual work with hands-on technical building. He spends his time conducting long-form interviews, traveling globally on spontaneous adventures, training grappling, and taking long hikes.

caption: I got to spend all day today with Jensen in Taiwan: talking with thousands of engineers and eating street food at a night market. Jensen is received as a rockstar in Taiwan, like it's Beatles in the 60's. It's mind-blowing and fun to watch. But most importantly, through all the interactions and all my conversations with him, he remained the same humble, kind, thoughtful, funny guy he always was, even as a kid who went to these same night markets many years ago. Btw, we tried a crazy amount of different street food. It's legit some of the most delicious food I've ever had. I can't wait to share | location: Taiwan | date: 2026-06-02

caption: I'm traveling the world for a bit, starting with China but then hopping around the globe, anywhere. Open to any adventure. No plans, only a backpack. Hoping to meet & get to know humans from all walks of life. The pic is from a long hike on the Great Wall. For me, as a fan of history, this was an epic experience. In China, first I'm visiting a few big cities & talking to engineers at the heart of China's AI revolution. After that, if feeling crazy enough, I'm hitchhiking (first time) across rural China for a few weeks. Hitchhiking because I think it's the best way to meet rural folks who I wou | date: 2026-05-14
caption: Love you all ❤️ | date: 2026-04-08

caption: It was an honor to hang out with Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, and do a long-form podcast with him. Really fun & fascinating technical deep-dive conversation on & off the mic. One of the most brilliant & thoughtful human beings I've ever met. NVIDIA is the most valuable company in the world by market cap and is the engine powering the AI revolution. Podcast probably out tomorrow (Monday), unless I get stuck in too many interesting conversations while running around in SF ;-) PS: I haven't checked my messages in days. Sorry for slow replies 🙏 Trying to stay deeply focused in an overwhelmingly i | date: 2026-03-22

caption: Here's a video of me training with @khabib_nurmagomedov, one of the greatest fighters of all time and a great human being. This was truly an honor for me 🙏 Full video is on YouTube. | date: 2026-03-02

caption: It might be the caffeine speaking, but I love you all ❤️ Happy Valentine's day you sexy mf'ers. I'm writing this at a coffeeshop. Rain outside. A first date happening next to me, I'm hoping they make it. I'm feeling happy & grateful for all of this, human civilization, life on Earth, a spinning rock in space. There are 100-400 billion other planets in our galaxy alone. And there are ~2 trillion galaxies in just the observable universe. And somehow we have a chance to crack open the mysteries of the universe, to solve physics, biology, intelligence, to understand our own mind, to travel out tow | date: 2026-02-14

caption: I got to train with @khabib_nurmagomedov yesterday. This was an honor of a lifetime for me. He's a great fighter & leader and a great human being. From a grappling perspective, I don't think I've ever experienced this much top pressure in my life. I'll post the footage of the training in a few days. And also we'll do a long podcast (and dub it in multiple languages). In general, it was an incredible experience to train with the team and get to know many of the fighters from Dagestan. All are great people. | date: 2026-01-22

caption: Long hike in LA hills with @hubermanlab, one of my favorite humans (& best friends) on Earth. I enjoy hikes where you can be in nature and still, at some high-elevation points, see the city in the distance below. In those moments, it all seems so surreal. How did we clever humans build all of that? We went from hunter-gatherers to a civilization that can space travel and has a chance to colonize other planets and reach out toward the stars 🤯 | date: 2025-12-16

caption: View of Earth from 900 million miles away, with Saturn's rings in the image, taken by Cassini spacecraft. That dot is us, all 8 billion of us. It's all an insanely lucky miracle. I'm grateful for all of it & all of you. Love you all! ❤️ PS: Now, I'm off to partake in the great American Thanksgiving tradition of over-eating while getting into a heated philosophical argument with family 🤣 | date: 2025-11-27

caption: Over the past several weeks, I've been back in the lab working crazy hours like old times, and loving life. This was much needed. I'm happy ;-) If I'm not programming, hands-on with robots/hardware for many hours a day, I feel a bit lost and less able to think clearly about the world. It's just how my brain is built. I think it's because engineering humbles me to the reality of the world. I need both literature & engineering in my life 🤣 I love both, and both are a source of truth. I'm still doing the podcast, just adding much more engineering back into the mix ;-) The podcast gives me an opp | date: 2025-11-05

caption: Feeling down about the world and about myself. Normal human things. I'm sure soon it'll be better. If you're down too, sending you love. I'm hiding from the world for a bit, enjoying the Boston fall months, long runs along the Charles river. I think humans are beautiful and fascinating and for the most part awesome. The internet seems to want to tell you otherwise. I disagree, but I don't have the right words for it. I'll probably do a long solo episode on Dostoevsky (especially Brothers Karamazov) at some point to help me articulate this better. I love you all. | date: 2025-10-04

caption: Thank you for the birthday wishes 🙏 I'm grateful for another year around the sun, on this strange little planet of ours, with all of you. I've traveled a lot this year, and got to meet & talk to many people from all walks of life. The more I did, the more optimism I gained for the future of humanity. We humans are a good bunch. I love you all ❤️ | date: 2025-08-15

One of the most brilliant & thoughtful human beings I've ever met. NVIDIA is the most valuable company in the world by market cap and is the engine powering the AI revolution. Podcast probably out tomorrow (Monday), unless I get stuck in too many interesting conversations while running around in SF ;-) PS: I haven't checked my messages in days. Sorry for slow replies 🙏 Trying to stay deeply focused in an overwhelmingly i
Here's a video of me training with @khabib_nurmagomedov, one of the greatest fighters of all time and a great human being. This was truly an honor for me 🙏 Full video is on YouTube.

It might be the caffeine speaking, but I love you all ❤️ Happy Valentine's day you sexy mf'ers. I'm writing this at a coffeeshop. Rain outside. A first date happening next to me, I'm hoping they make it. I'm feeling happy & grateful for all of this, human civilization, life on Earth, a spinning rock in space. There are 100-400 billion other planets in our galaxy alone. And there are ~2 trillion galaxies in just the observable universe. And somehow we have a chance to crack open the mysteries of the universe, to solve physics, biology, intelligence, to understand our own mind, to travel out tow

I got to train with @khabib_nurmagomedov yesterday. This was an honor of a lifetime for me. He's a great fighter & leader and a great human being. From a grappling perspective, I don't think I've ever experienced this much top pressure in my life. I'll post the footage of the training in a few days. And also we'll do a long podcast (and dub it in multiple languages). In general, it was an incredible experience to train with the team and get to know many of the fighters from Dagestan. All are great people.

Long hike in LA hills with @hubermanlab, one of my favorite humans (& best friends) on Earth. I enjoy hikes where you can be in nature and still, at some high-elevation points, see the city in the distance below. In those moments, it all seems so surreal. How did we clever humans build all of that? We went from hunter-gatherers to a civilization that can space travel and has a chance to colonize other planets and reach out toward the stars 🤯

View of Earth from 900 million miles away, with Saturn's rings in the image, taken by Cassini spacecraft. That dot is us, all 8 billion of us. It's all an insanely lucky miracle. I'm grateful for all of it & all of you. Love you all! ❤️ PS: Now, I'm off to partake in the great American Thanksgiving tradition of over-eating while getting into a heated philosophical argument with family 🤣

Over the past several weeks, I've been back in the lab working crazy hours like old times, and loving life. This was much needed. I'm happy ;-) If I'm not programming, hands-on with robots/hardware for many hours a day, I feel a bit lost and less able to think clearly about the world. It's just how my brain is built. I think it's because engineering humbles me to the reality of the world. I need both literature & engineering in my life 🤣 I love both, and both are a source of truth. I'm still doing the podcast, just adding much more engineering back into the mix ;-) The podcast gives me an opp

Feeling down about the world and about myself. Normal human things. I'm sure soon it'll be better. If you're down too, sending you love. I'm hiding from the world for a bit, enjoying the Boston fall months, long runs along the Charles river. I think humans are beautiful and fascinating and for the most part awesome. The internet seems to want to tell you otherwise. I disagree, but I don't have the right words for it. I'll probably do a long solo episode on Dostoevsky (especially Brothers Karamazov) at some point to help me articulate this better. I love you all.

Thank you for the birthday wishes 🙏 I'm grateful for another year around the sun, on this strange little planet of ours, with all of you. I've traveled a lot this year, and got to meet & talk to many people from all walks of life. The more I did, the more optimism I gained for the future of humanity. We humans are a good bunch. I love you all ❤️

Brené Brown is a research professor at the University of Houston, where she holds the Huffington Foundation Endowed Chair at the Graduate College of Social Work. She also holds the position of Professor of Practice in Management at The University of Texas at Austin McCombs School of Business.Brené is the author of six #1 New York Times bestsellers and the host of two award-winning podcasts. Brené spends most of her time working in organizations around the world, helping develop braver leaders and more courageous cultures. In 2024, she was named Executive Chair of the Center for Daring Leadership at BetterUp. She lives in Houston, Texas, with her husband, Steve. They have two children, Ellen
Professor of Practice @ The University of Texas at Austin - Red McCombs School of Business (Jan 2020 - Present 6 years 10 months)

Founder @ Brené Brown Education and Research Group (2016 - Present 10 years) — The mission of Brené Brown Education and Research Group (BBEARG) is to develop and deliver accessible, relevant, and research-based offerings to individuals, families, communities, organizations, and schools so that people have the emotional, cognitive, and behavioral foundation they need to show up, be seen, and live braver lives.

snippets.text: 👨‍⚕️ Doctor-turned-Entrepreneur + Productivity Expert + YouTuber (6M subs) 📘 New York Times Bestselling Author of “Feel-Good Productivity”
London, England, United Kingdom

I’m Ali, a YouTuber, podcaster, author of New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller, Feel-Good Productivity, and ex-Doctor working in London, UK.

I make videos that explore the strategies and tools that help us live happier, healthier and more productive lives. I also have a weekly podcast called Deep Dive and I write a weekly email newsletter that contains some quick thoughts + links to interesting things.

I studied Medicine for 6 years at Cambridge University, and graduated in 2018. On my YouTube channel (4.5 million subscribers) I make videos about medicine, tech and productivity. 

📚 Check out my New York Times Bestselling Book Feel-Good Productivity: https://go.feelgoodproductivity.

snippets.text: Founder: Steven.com The Creator Economy Company, home to FlightStory & FlightCast.
3M followers

Steven Bartlett is a 33-year-old British entrepreneur, investor in more than 100 companies, speaker, author, and media owner. He is the founder of Steven.com - the creator media company. Through it's podcast creator "label" called FlightStory, they create and scales new media podcast IP and commercialise that IP through brand partnerships, programmatic revenue, events, book publishing, newsletters, e-commerce, and new product development.He is also the co-founder of thirdweb, a developer platform powering over 100,000 teams to build and launch web3 applications, and FlightCast, a video-first podcast hosting platform used by some of the world’s largest shows.Steven first gained recognition as

Founder & CEO @ Steven.com (Nov 2025 - Present 1 year) — Steven.com is the creator economy company. We build and own businesses across every layer of it: media, technology, commerce, community and events. Home to some of the biggest creator IP and most advanced creator technology in the world. London, Manchester, New York and LA.

Founder @ FLIGHTSTORY (Jan 2025 - Present 1 year 10 months) — FlightStory is a creator media company and the home of The Diary of a CEO - With Steven Bartlett, We Need To Talk With Paul Brunson, Begin Again With Davina McCall, Hot Smart Rich With Maggie Sellers and 30 other creators. We produce long-form media IP that had reached billions globally.

Co-Founder @ Flightcast (May 2024 - Present 2 years 6 months) — A few years ago we got annoyed that all the podcast hosting platforms were inadequate and built for the past. So myself and Rox built a better one, which is built for the future. FlightCast is an AI-powered distribution platform built for podcast creators. It automates publishing, optimises content for each platform, and gives creators the infrastructure to grow without the operational overhead. www.flightcast.com. It's now used by many of the world's biggest shows.

Co-Owner @ Chapter 2 (Jul 2024 - Present 2 years 4 months) — 8 years ago I met Leo Harrison before Chapter2 was founded, and we wanted to start a company together. We couldn't quite decide what to start, but ultimately he came back to me some years later with Chapter2 and I became the companies sole investor and partner. The company now employs hundreds of people and drives the talent function for some of the world's leading brands.
Co-owner @ Ketone-IQ (Jan 2025 - Present 1 year 10 months)
Founder @ The Diary Of A CEO (Jan 2020 - Present 6 years 10 months) — I started a podcast and it got out of hand.

Investor & Partner @ PerfectTed (Jan 2022 - Present 4 years 10 months) — PerfectTed is the UK’s fastest growing founder led company according to a recent report. They are also Europe’s leading Matcha brand. I was the first investor and partner, having invested £1m± into the company - they’ve recently exceeded $100m annual run rate and are on track to become the world’s biggest matcha brand. They are also Dragons Den's most successful ever deal.
Investor @ Neko Health (Jan 2026 - Present 10 months) — Invested $2.8m into Neko Health to help build the infrastructure for preventable health care.
Investor @ Lovable (Jan 2025 - Present 1 year 10 months)

Investor @ Stan (Apr 2025 - Present 1 year 7 months) — Empowering the next generation of creator-entrepreneurs. I joined Stan as an investor to help scale the most accessible platform for monetising digital audiences. From strategy to storytelling, I’m supporting Stan’s mission to make financial freedom possible for anyone with a smartphone and an idea.
Investor @ SpaceX (Jan 2024 - Present 2 years 10 months) — Invested in SpaceX as a private company at a roughly $150b± valuation. SpaceX would later IPO reaching a $3T valuation.

Investor @ Wispr Flow (Jan 2025 - Present 1 year 10 months) — Become a shareholder, investor and partner in Wispr Flow early in the companies story after personally reaching out to the companies founders. This year the company closed a large investment round at a $2B valuation, led by Menlo Ventures, with Goodwater Capital, Forerunner, and Acrew Capital joining as major investors, alongside an incredible group of other funds, angels, and a few celebrities.

Philanthropist, businesswoman, author, and global advocate for women & girls. Founder of Pivotal. Co-founder of the Gates Foundation. Author of The Moment of Lift.

Founder @ Pivotal (2015 - Present 11 years) — Pivotal, which I founded in 2015, works to accelerate the pace of social progress for women and young people in the U.S. and around the world. Pivotal includes Pivotal Philanthropies, Pivotal Initiatives Fund, and Pivotal Ventures.

Co-Founder & Co-Chair @ Gates Foundation (2000 - 2024 24 years) — As co-founder and co-chair, I set the direction and priorities of the foundation. Specifically, I concentrated on family planning, maternal and child health, and applying the principles of user-centered design to the field of global health and development.
Board of Trustees Member @ Duke University (1996 - 2003 7 years)

General Manager of Information Products @ Microsoft (1987 - 1996 9 years) — During my time at Microsoft, I managed teams that developed multimedia and interactive products including Expedia, Cinemania and Encarta.

Being busy is a form of laziness—lazy thinking and indiscriminate action.
This should be the country where the most talented people in the world are coming to right now.
Being busy is a form of laziness—lazy thinking and indiscriminate action.
Do not overestimate the competition and underestimate yourself. You are better than you think.
I’ve gathered practical insights from @chipconley, @gregorymckeown, David Allen, @elizabeth_gilbert_writer, and @oliverburkeman_.
Why you need to workshop your ideas in person.

personality.communication_style: Direct, structured, and curious, often sharing curated questions, quotes, and distilled takeaways.
personality.humor: Dry, analytical, and grounded in questioning common societal habits.
personality.energy: Measured and focused, favoring purposeful engagement over chaotic activity.

lifestyle.pace: Deliberate and reflective; consciously avoids being swept up by busywork.
lifestyle.travel: Not stated in sources
lifestyle.routine: Structured around podcasting, newsletter writing, investing, and taking intentional time for weekends.

ambitions: Understanding and sharing playbooks behind world-first breakthroughs and policy changes.
Guiding people toward simplifying their lives using tested, practical insights.
looking_for: A partner who values focused intention over reactive busyness.
Someone interested in testing, simplifying, and workshopping ideas together in person.
An intellectually grounded companion who appreciates quiet reflection as much as deep inquiry.
green_flags: Willingness to simplify life and prune unnecessary obligations.
Appreciation for direct, in-person discussions rather than superficial exchanges.
Confidence in their own capabilities and mutual support.
friction_points: May become frustrated by persistent chaos, chronic over-scheduling, or glorification of being busy.
A strong preference for dissecting and workshopping concepts could feel overly analytical in casual moments.
dealbreakers: Chronic addiction to indiscriminate busyness without desire to simplify (low confidence inference).
Aversion to deep in-person discussion and creative problem-solving (low confidence inference).
dossier.ideal_date: Meeting up in person for coffee or an unhurried walk to workshop a curious idea or talk through ways to simplify life.
openers: What is one practical habit you have used lately to simplify your life?
How do you typically protect your time from indiscriminate busyness?
If we had an afternoon to workshop an unconventional idea in person, what would we tackle?
voice: Being busy is a form of laziness—lazy thinking and indiscriminate action.
Do not overestimate the competition and underestimate yourself. You are better than you think.
Please enjoy!

NEW podcast episode is up! “How to Legalize Medical Psychedelics in Your Country — Tania de Jong on The Playbook Behind Australia’s World-First Breakthrough” My guest today is Tania de Jong (@TaniadeJongam), co-founder of Mind Medicine Australia (@mindmedicine.au). Tania and her husband, Peter, helped lead the push that, in 2023, made Australia the first country in the world to allow MDMA and psilocybin to be prescribed for psychiatric conditions. I wanted to understand how the hell they helped make that happen and what the rest of the world can learn from it. Please enjoy!
